sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Brings in React for building the screen, the data fetching tool, and the helper that calls the server.
sections.why: Standard setup for a screen that loads data from the server.

sections.name: SlideRef
sections.title: Slide reference shape
sections.what: Describes one slide in the deck that shows an item, with its position, id, kind and title.
sections.why: Gives the screen a fixed shape for slide data so it reads it safely.

sections.name: Item, Coverage
sections.title: Item and coverage data shapes
sections.what: Describes one piece of evidence used in a Lessons Learnt run, including its kind, where it was routed, whether it was admitted, the slides it appears on and its source link. Also describes the whole response for a project, with its runs and items.
sections.why: Gives the screen a fixed shape for the data it receives from the server.
sections.watch_out: The screen trusts this shape without checking at run time, so a server change that renames a field would show blanks silently.

sections.name: BASIS_LABEL, VER_LABEL
sections.title: Plain labels for internal codes
sections.what: Turns internal codes such as keyword or unverified into phrases shown to the user, such as Source unreachable or No pillar matched.
sections.why: Likely reason: so the owner can read why evidence was routed without knowing the internal names.
sections.watch_out: A new code that is not in these tables will show as raw text, so add it when the server adds one.

sections.name: Slides
sections.title: Slide labels
sections.what: Shows the slide numbers where an item appears as small labels, with the slide title as a tooltip. Shows Not on a slide when there are none.
sections.why: So a reader can move from a finding to the slide that uses it.
sections.watch_out: The slide kind is shown with underscores replaced by spaces, so unusual kind names will look odd.

sections.name: ItemRow
sections.title: One evidence table row
sections.what: Builds one table row per item: the excerpt, a note on its type and source link, the sub-driver code, how it was routed, its source check, and the slides it appears on.
sections.why: Keeps the layout of each row in one place.
sections.watch_out: An item with no excerpt leaves the main column blank.

sections.name: LessonsCoverageTab (part 1)
sections.title: Main screen, run picker and grouping
sections.what: Fetches the coverage for one project and shows a loading message or an error. If no run has covered the project, it says so. Otherwise it lets the user pick a run, shows four summary figures, and groups the used items by pillar.
sections.why: Likely reason: to show how each run used a project's evidence, in one place.
sections.watch_out: If the chosen run is no longer in the data, the screen silently falls back to the first run.

sections.name: LessonsCoverageTab (part 2)
sections.title: Held items toggle
sections.what: A button that shows or hides the evidence that was collected but not used, with the reason each one was held back.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond keeping the main view focused on what was used.
sections.watch_out: Held items are hidden by default, so a reader may not realise rejected evidence exists unless they press the button.

summary: A panel on a project page that shows which Lessons Learnt runs used the project's evidence, where each piece was filed, and whether it was checked against its source.
purpose: Lets the owner audit how the lessons tool used each fact, finding and commentary item for a project.
why: The header says nothing here is recalculated. The screen only displays what the server's coverage ledger recorded.
how: 1. Ask the server for the coverage of this project. 2. Show a loading, error or empty message when needed. 3. Pick the chosen run, defaulting to the first. 4. Split items into used and held. 5. Group used items by pillar and show a table for each. 6. Offer a toggle to reveal held items and their reasons.
inputs: The project id from the parent page, and the coverage response from the lessons coverage endpoint.
outputs: A panel with a run picker, four summary figures, one table per pillar and a hidden list of held items. Nothing is saved.
risks: The screen displays whatever the server sends without checking it, so a changed response can show wrong figures. Unknown codes appear as raw text.
debug: If the panel is empty, check that a run exists for the project. If figures look wrong, compare with the coverage ledger on the server. Check the browser network tab for the lessons-coverage request. If a code shows raw, add it to the label tables.
